entries.name: Mummichog
behaviour: darts in schools through tidal pools and marsh creeks
tolerates huge salinity swings, from fresh to twice seawater
classic aquarium killifish, striped with silvery bars

voxel_model.pattern: silvery vertical bars on olive flanks

entries.notes: The default minnow of tidal creeks; survives being stranded in hypersaline pools at low tide.

entries.name: Pinfish
behaviour: shiny silvery-green swarms in surf and jetties
steals baited hooks as it is the commonest bycatch of pier anglers
common in seagrass beds and estuaries as well

voxel_model.pattern: five faint vertical bars, yellow fins

entries.notes: The shiny nuisance of bait shops and piers; every saltwater beginner catches pinfish first. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Common ringed plover
entries.migrates: northern breeders winter on European and African coasts
behaviour: bold black breast band and orange legs; runs and freezes like its kin
nests in a shallow scrape above the tide line on shingle or sand
broken-wing distraction display when nest is threatened

voxel_model.pattern: black band across chest and forehead

entries.notes: Europe's answer to the piping plover; same run-stop-freeze choreography on pale sand. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Kentish plover
behaviour: pale ghost on open salt-pan and beach scraped hollows
males defend nest scrape with wing-quivering displays
nests on open shelly sand far from vegetation

voxel_model.pattern: incomplete dark breast band on males

entries.notes: Small pale plover of open sandy coasts worldwide; once nested on Kentish beaches, hence the name. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Dunlin
behaviour: chestnut back and black belly patch in breeding plumage
probes mud with drooping bill in vast flocks on tidal flats
rocks forward and back while feeding in dense groups
entries.notes: The quintessential Arctic-breeding shorebird of winter tidal flats; black-bellied and chestnut in summer. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Least sandpiper
behaviour: smallest peep of the Americas; yellow-green legs
picks daintily along the wrack line
crouches flat when threatened, vanishing into sand texture

voxel_model.pattern: rufous back, white underparts, yellow legs

entries.notes: The tiniest dash of movement on the beach; look for yellow legs among its grey-legged cousins. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Western sandpiper
behaviour: scans mudflats with slight downcurved bill while foraging
huge spring passage flocks stop at estuary hotspots
rufous shoulder patches in spring plumage

voxel_model.pattern: rufous scapulars in spring, black legs

entries.notes: The American west-coast counterpart of the semipalmated sandpiper; probe-walking clouds of small peeps. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Grey plover
behaviour: stocky silvery plover; black belly and face in summer dress
melancholy drawn-out whistle on southern winter shores
runs in bursts then stands bolt upright scanning for worms

voxel_model.pattern: black belly in breeding plumage, white rump in flight

entries.notes: The stocky grey-and-black plover of winter beaches worldwide; called black-bellied plover in the Americas. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Little egret
behaviour: snow-white egret with wispy nape plumes and golden slipper feet
runs forward through shallows stirring fish then strikes
colonises heronries, mixing with grey herons and cattle egrets
sounds: hoarse croaking and squawking in colonies

voxel_model.pattern: long nape plumes and gaudy yellow feet

entries.notes: The Old World's answer to the snowy egret; expanding north in a warming Europe. gestation_days is incubation.

entries.name: Harbour porpoise
behaviour: small shy cetacean with blunt rounded head and no beak
low rolling swim; rarely breaches, just surfaces and sinks
frequents bays and estuaries; feeds close to shore
sounds: ultrasonic clicks for echolocation; sneezing exhale
entries.notes: The smallest porpoise and the commonest near-shore cetacean of the Northern Hemisphere; quiet and easy to miss.

entries.name: Capelin
entries.migrates: mass spawning migrations onto sandy beaches
behaviour: millions beach themselves at high-tide nights to spawn on sand
males ridge with iridescent flanks during the rolling runs
spawning on the beach is near-100 percent fatal for males
sounds: unearthly squeaking and rasping during beach runs

voxel_model.pattern: olive back, silver flanks, reddish nape

entries.notes: A grunion-like northern fish; famous Newfoundland beach spawning runs draw whales, cod, gulls and fishers alike.

entries.name: Pacific sand lance
behaviour: buries itself tail-first in clean bottom sand to overnight
waves in huge silvery shoals at slack tide or when fleeing
no swim bladder; sinks and rests on sand by day

voxel_model.pattern: long eel-like silvery body, pointed beak

entries.notes: The eel-like keystone forage fish; it fuels salmon, seabird colonies and humpback bubble-net hunts. gestation_days is larval incubation.

entries.name: Sheepshead minnow
behaviour: tough little pupfish of hypersaline pools and marsh creeks
males turn steel-blue with a dark side bar in spawning dress
classic lab-rat fish; breeds readily in captivity
entries.notes: The stocky little pupfish of the salty edge; tolerates heat, salt and crowding with ease.

entries.name: European green crab
behaviour: five points on each side of the carapace; world's worst invasive crab
crushes shellfish beds, ripping mussels off their byssus
tolerates salt from 4 to 52 parts per thousand
entries.notes: The alien invader wrecking shellfish beds on three continents; five lateral spines per side give it away. gestation_days is larval incubation.

entries.name: Asian shore crab
behaviour: small square crab with bright orange banding on the claws
swarms rock jetties and pilings in astronomical numbers
invasive in western Atlantic since 1988
entries.notes: The sudden orange-clawed invader of Atlantic jetties; outcompetes nothing but pours out of every crevice. gestation_days is larval incubation.

entries.name: Striped shore crab
behaviour: green-to-purple square crab striped like a miniature tiger
scrambles sideways over rocks above the surf line
climbs high on pilings and driftwood to escape the waves
entries.notes: The striped rock-skipper of Pacific jetties; too quick to catch and too tough to bother with.

entries.name: Caribbean land hermit crab
behaviour: occupies scavenged snail shells above the wrack line
climbs palm trunks; drowns in salt water when trapped
must return to the sea to release larvae

voxel_model.pattern: spiral shell worn as armour, purple-brown claws

entries.notes: The palm-climbing beach hermit; pet-shop favourite that needs the ocean for its young. gestation_days is larval incubation.

entries.name: Common periwinkle
behaviour: climbs rocks above the tide line to escape predators
grazes films of algae with a rasping radula
swarms in dense bands along the mid-tide zone
entries.notes: The winkles of chip-shop and pier; a dark banded spiral grazed off the mid-shore rocks. gestation_days is larval incubation.

entries.name: Blue mussel
behaviour: clusters in dense carpets on rocks, groynes and jetties
anchors with tough byssus threads to ride out the surf
farmed worldwide as the everyday eating mussel
entries.notes: The everyday eating mussel; rope-grown and wild carpets alike pave the low-tide rocks.

entries.name: Common limpet
behaviour: rasps algae with one of the hardest teeth in nature
grips rock with a suction foot so hard it cannot be pulled off
homing scar in the rock returns worn smoother each visit
entries.notes: The rock-clamped volcano of the mid-shore; iron-tipped teeth make its radula nature's hardest known material.

entries.name: Common cockle
behaviour: heart-shaped ribbed shell buried just under the sand surface
jumps short distances by flicking its foot
classic bait and seafood of European sandy estuaries
entries.notes: The ribbed little bivalve of spring tides; staple bait and seafood of the shellfish-gathering shore.

entries.name: Pacific razor clam
behaviour: buries itself 30 cm down and jets a telltale plume of water
diggers chase the dimple left behind at swash edge
fast burrow favoured by surf-zone anglers
entries.notes: The diggable clam of Washington and Oregon surf beaches; a perfect digging contest prey.

entries.name: Lugworm
behaviour: leaves coiled casts of swallowed sand on the flat at low tide
lives in a U-shaped burrow up to 40 cm deep
sold worldwide as universal fishing bait; called sandworm
entries.notes: The bait-digger's grail; those cast coils on cold European beaches are its burrow's calling card. gestation_days is larval incubation.

entries.name: Talitrus sandhopper
entries.migrates: hops up and down the beach with the tides
behaviour: catapults itself sideways by flexing the tail section
burrows into damp sand at the high-tide line by day
the original European 'sand flea' under beach towels
entries.notes: The hopping half of every beach picnic; cleaner of wrack but nip-happy under towels.

entries.name: Sea slater
behaviour: runs flat-out over rocks like a small grey tank
lives under stones above the tide line, fully terrestrial
mother carries the brood in a pouch until they scatter

voxel_model.pattern: grey oval armoured segments, long feelers

entries.notes: The big woodlouse of seaside rocks; a shuffling, armoured rumour that the tide has already come and gone.

entries.name: Kelp fly
behaviour: swarms black clouds over rotting stranded kelp
breeds inside the wet wrack line itself; larvae feed on decaying algae
bites itch badly enough that beaches post warnings
entries.notes: The biting black storm over the wrack line; the reason nobody sunbathes on fresh kelp casts.

entries.name: Ghost shrimp
eats: organic particles from burrow water currents
behaviour: invisible in its U-burrow; reveals itself by squirting a sand volcano
sand flats are riddled with their feeding-mound shafts
useless as direct catch; beloved classic aquarium scavenger
entries.notes: The invisible tenant of muddy-sand flats; every collapse-hole in the tideflat is a volcano of its burrow.

entries.name: Neverita moon snail
behaviour: drills a neat countersunk hole through clam shells to reach the meat
hides in a huge balloon-like foot under the sand
sand collar egg cases look like miniature coffee filters
entries.notes: The sand-bulldozer predator; its drilled-clam shells are the most common beach-collected sign of snail violence.

entries.name: Dog whelk
behaviour: drills barnacles and mussels with a rasping radula and acid saliva
yellow egg capsules glued in clusters to rocks and kelp
can change shell colour from banded to solid with diet
entries.notes: The deliberate snail of the upper shore; its drilled barnacle plates are the calling card of the low-tide robbery.

entries.name: Beach wolf spider
behaviour: hides in a silk-lined burrow in dry upper sand
greenish-brown with darker marbling; too fast and skittish to grab
female carries the egg sac at her spinnerets, then the spiderlings on her back
entries.notes: The big eight-eyed runner of open US beaches; it watches you from its burrow with unnerving patience.

entries.name: Heart urchin
behaviour: heart-shaped, densely spined buried just under the sand
leaves a tell-tale dent and scattered spines after storms
flattened unlike round sea urchins; built for burrowing
entries.notes: The heart-shaped ghost of the buried sand; its outline shows in shells washed onto the wrack line.

entries.name: Sand bubbler crab
behaviour: sweeps the swash with one claw and rolls sand into perfect spheres
millions of sand pellets give the flat a fresh-popped-rice look
disappears into a popcorn-burrow in an instant when disturbed
entries.notes: The infinite small-sphere factory of tropical flats; thousands of pellets mark its grazing on low tide.

entries.name: California sea hare
behaviour: giant slug-like mollusc with rabbit-ear rhinophores
inks purple when harassed; unpalatable and foul
the neuron lab animal of choice for memory research

voxel_model.pattern: mottled brown-purple with dark inking skin

entries.notes: The jumbo laboratory bunny-ears of algae flats; ink the water purple and nobody eats you.

entries.name: Sand wasp
behaviour: digs flask-shaped burrows in open sand in full sun
paralyses flies mid-air and drags them underground as nursery food
nesting females hover like tiny fighter jets over their burrow
entries.notes: The hornet-like sand raptor; every burrow is a fly-filled pantry guarded at hover-speed.

entries.name: Salt marsh biting midge
behaviour: clouds bite through bug spray at dawn and dusk near salt marshes
larvae develop in salty marsh mud, not standing fresh water
leaves clusters of itchy welts worse than mosquito bites

voxel_model.pattern: tiny dark biting fly with spotted wings

entries.notes: The no-see-um of every salt-marsh evening; unseen, unrelenting, and unforgettable at picnics.
